chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
A man’s vanity for himself is one of the enemies of his intelligence.
ai.seo_question: What is the effect of self-vanity on human intelligence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) characterizes self-admiration (ujb) not merely as a moral flaw but as an internal saboteur of intellect, effectively acting as a 'jealous rival' that blinds the mind to truth. This concept is central to Shia ethical psychology, where ujb is distinguished from simple pride by its subtle, insidious nature that erodes self-awareness and intellectual humility. The metaphor of the 'jealous one' highlights how vanity actively competes with reason, preventing the individual from achieving the clarity required for spiritual and intellectual growth.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 212. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
A man’s vanity for himself is one of the enemies of his intelligence. [1]
